result:
**Chosen approach:** used the existing `assumption_disclosure`/escalation concept already present in the response (`escalation_needed`, `escalation_reasons` at the pipeline level, and `escalation_recommended`/`computation_trace` per deadline row via `assumption_disclosures`) — no public API shape change needed, per the scope rule preferring that option when such a field already exists.

**What was wrong:** in `pipeline.py:99-112`, if the `court_closures` fetch raised an exception, the failure was only logged; `closure_dates` silently fell back to an empty frozenset and computation proceeded as though closures were simply unknown/absent, indistinguishable from a legitimate empty result. For fatal-severity deadlines this happened to still trigger escalation (via the pre-existing `has_local_closure_data` check), but the escalation reason said "no local court closure data is available" — masking that it was actually a system fetch failure — and for non-fatal deadlines there was no flag or escalation at all, so a deadline could be silently computed and written using only synthetic statewide holidays with no indication anything was amiss.

**What changed:** added a `closure_fetch_failed` flag set in the `except` block. When true, every computed deadline for that document gets an explicit assumption disclosure ("Court closure data could not be retrieved (system error)...") appended to `deadline.assumption_disclosures`, and `should_escalate` is forced `True` regardless of rule severity or confidence — surfacing via the existing `escalation_needed`/`escalation_reasons` fields returned by `/api/deadline/analyze/{document_id}`. No date math changed.

**What could regress:** if a caller relied on `escalation_needed` staying `False` for non-fatal deadlines even when the DB was flaky, it will now see more escalations during closure-fetch outages — this is intentional per the "fail or flag, never guess" doctrine. Verified with a new test file `tests/test_deadline_pipeline.py` (failed before the fix, passes after), and the full CI-scope suite is green (198 passed, 1 skipped).

Noted in FOLLOW_UPS.md: nothing extra observed outside scope — the fix stayed within `pipeline.py`.
